name: North Buttress (Thread of Gneiss)
approach: From the Lower Goodell Creek trailhead, day one covers more than six miles and 6,000 feet of elevation gain to a col near the Chopping Block. Day two crosses snow, slabs, and talus through Crescent Creek Basin, then crampons up to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, followed by one rappel down onto the Mustard Glacier to reach the base of the North Buttress.
overview: A nine-pitch, 2,000-foot buttress route up East Twin Needle's north side, first climbed in 2022 along a line envisioned decades earlier by North Cascades historian John Roper.
beta: Most pitches run out beyond 250 feet and are simul-climbed on solid, clean Skagit gneiss. The route favors the right side of the buttress low down, following the rib left of a gully to the top of the first tower, before a crux 8th pitch that combines a chimney, a leftward rising traverse across a face, and an exposed arête requiring careful, sometimes lichen-coated 5.9 moves.
fa: Eric Wehrly and Sam Boyce, July 31, 2022 (line named "Thread of Gneiss" by John Roper in 1981, first climbed in 2022)
